A string the master list has never seen is remembered in memory before any file is touched, and the write of Master.txt that follows it can fail without taking the application down, because the save path is not always a place this process may write: an installed app's static data sits in a bundle nobody can write to, and a path that was only ever correct on one developer's machine resolves somewhere absurd everywhere else - in both shapes Directory.CreateDirectory or the Master_new.txt write threw out of AddNewString, out of Translate, and out of whatever was drawing the first screen that displayed a new piece of text, which is every run after a feature adds a string since Master.txt is deliberately regenerated rather than committed. The machineTranslation.Add now happens first and unconditionally, so the string translates to itself for the rest of the run and, being in the map, brings the doomed write around exactly once per new string instead of once per draw; the disk work underneath it catches IOException, UnauthorizedAccessException, NotSupportedException and ArgumentException - the four ways a bad path announces itself, with DirectoryNotFoundException arriving as the first of them - and writes the save path and the message to Debug.WriteLine as the rest of agg reports what it chose to survive, rather than rethrowing. Recreated after the worktree holding the original 307fa983 was removed and the commit went with it.
